gen.title: How carbon dioxide uptake changes ocean chemistry and marine life
gen.orderNote: Arrange events in the order the chemistry changes are taught

steps.label: Ocean takes in atmospheric carbon dioxide
steps.quote: The ocean absorbs about 30 percent of the CO2 that is released in the atmosphere

steps.label: Seawater chemistry produces more hydrogen ions
steps.quote: When CO2 is absorbed by seawater, a series of chemical reactions occur resulting in the increased concentration of hydrogen ions.

steps.label: Seawater turns more acidic and loses carbonate
steps.quote: This increase causes the seawater to become more acidic and causes carbonate ions to be relatively less abundant.

steps.label: Shell building grows harder for calcifying organisms
steps.quote: Decreases in carbonate ions can make building and maintaining shells and other calcium carbonate structures difficult for calcifying organisms

steps.label: Fish lose ability to sense predators
steps.quote: Certain fish's ability to detect predators is decreased in more acidic waters.

steps.label: Entire food web faces growing risk
steps.quote: When these organisms are at risk, the entire food web may also be at risk.
